claims.text: The balance between configurational entropy, lattice strain, and intermetallic interactions governs structural and chemical stability in equiatomic multimetal nanoparticles.
Smaller nanoparticles have lower lattice-strain energy than larger nanoparticles of the same composition.
Lower lattice-strain energy allows configurational entropy to maintain a single-phase solid solution from 473 K to 1923 K.
Larger nanoparticles have increased lattice strain that favors phase segregation under otherwise identical thermal conditions.
The target nanoparticles initially contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and are crystallized as a single-phase solid solution.
Nanoparticle size modulates lattice-strain energy when composition and synthesis protocol are held constant.
Intermetallic bonding interactions are amplified at higher lattice-strain energy.
Ordering and intermetallic interactions can drive multicomponent alloys from disordered solid solutions toward distinct crystalline or intermetallic states.
Enhanced lattice strain and intermetallic bonding in larger nanoparticles reduce the effectiveness of entropic stabilization.
Reduced entropic stabilization triggers phase segregation and secondary-phase formation during high-temperature operation.
Small nanoparticles will retain a single-phase structure throughout 473–1923 K.
Larger nanoparticles will exhibit phase segregation at a lower temperature than smaller nanoparticles.
Segregation in larger nanoparticles will be observable as additional crystalline phases and changes in lattice parameters.
The minimally sized nanoparticles constitute a baseline with minimal lattice strain and no detectable secondary phases over 473–1923 K.
The predicted size trend is conditional on minimizing surface-driven segregation and controlling processing and ambient conditions.
Surface oxidation or composition changes during thermal cycling may cause deviations from the predicted size trend.
The nanoparticle-size threshold for loss of entropic stabilization varies with the particular metal combination.
Surface-energy and other nanoscale effects may introduce variability into the relationship between particle size and stability.
